questions.sentence: Did you sell any securities whose basis was not reported to the IRS?
questions.assessment: 8949 boxes B/E concern securities with basis not reported; a personal item is not evidence of a securities sale.

questions.name: exception1.only-box2a-capital-gains
questions.sentence: Is it true that you had no capital gains in 2025 other than capital gain distributions in box 2a of Form 1099-DIV, and that you had no sale in 2025 of stock, bonds, funds or other property that you must report on Form 8949 or Schedule D (even one with no gain or loss)? Sales inside an IRA or 401(k) do not count, and neither does a loss on a personal item unless you received a Form 1099-S for it or you report it on Form 8949.
questions.assessment: The adopted v3 sentence expressly excludes a personal loss only when it is not reported on Form 8949 (and no Form 1099-S). This case is reported there. Exception 1 yes would contradict it.

questions.assessment: Personal-use property is a capital asset; a loss can be nondeductible and still require reporting and a positive code-L adjustment. Do not turn that item into the supported deductible securities loss.

conclusion: The eight sentences are valid domain questions, but the four added Exception 1 questions are not truthful additional ways to resolve this fixed personal-loss case. Preserve its four names. The no-form8949-sources answer (no here, yes on the four recorded target returns) distinguishes them inside the guard.
limit: Counterfactual answers demonstrate software routing, not permission to change truthful facts. No new question wording or personal-loss support is proposed.
